description:
Job Summary
Afghanistan
With more than 20 years of experience in the country, UNOPS Afghanistan focuses on providing maximum support to the people of Afghanistan through the delivery of projects and services that improve the lives of people in need. The UNOPS Afghanistan Country Office (AFCO) serves as an organizational mechanism to deliver a range of projects for which UNOPS has been designated as the implementation agency. At present, UNOPS AFCO activities cover a range of sectors including humanitarian, basic human needs, cash for work, infrastructure, development, procurement and HR services.
The functional objective of UNOPS AFCO is to contribute to improving the lives of girls, boys, men and women living in Afghanistan. The aim of UNOPS AFCO is to provide efficient and cost-effective implementation services on behalf of all our partners to support the humanitarian response and development of the country. UNOPS AFCO’s mission is to exceed the expectations of all stakeholders in the delivery of AFCO services, at all times, in all places, in all circumstances, in order to improve the lives of Afghans in need.

Job Requirements
Job Specific Context
This position is operates within the Afghanistan Country Office (AFCO) under the Programme Implementation Unit of the Afghanistan's Community Resilience and Livelihood Project (ACRLP). The role is critical for the operationalization, maintenance, and management of MIS databases, websites, and applications, ensuring smooth data operations for a large-scale community resilience program. Under the direct supervision of the ICT Specialist, the Information Management Officer will be responsible for the operationalization, maintenance and management and smooth operations of the databases, websites and applications.The incumbent will provide essential support and training to Facilitating Partners (FPs) and private contractors on the use of the Management Information System (MIS), directly contributing to the efficiency and effectiveness of humanitarian and development efforts in Afghanistan.

The Information Management Officer is responsible for the design, development, maintenance, and operational use of the Management Information System (MIS) and related data systems for the ACRLP project. S/he ensures effective integration with external systems, manages data quality, provides operational support and training to partners, and supervises MIS support staff. This role is crucial for enhancing the quality and accessibility of project data, facilitating timely reporting, and strengthening transparency and financial oversight to ensure program effectiveness and accountability.

Support capacity-building activities for staff and partners on MIS tools, data collection, GIS, and reporting.

title: Data Analysis and Validation Officer
description:
Role Summary
Background and Objective of the assignment
The Relief, Employment and Vital Infrastructure for the Vulnerable in Emergencies (REVIVE) Project, funded by the Government of the Republic of Korea (ROK) and implemented by UNDP, seeks to support vulnerable populations through employment generation, livelihood recovery, rehabilitation of community infrastructure, and resilience-building initiatives. The project contributes to improving socio-economic conditions, strengthening community resilience, and increasing access to sustainable livelihood opportunities, particularly for women, youth, and vulnerable households.
To support effective Programme implementation, monitoring, and accountability, UNDP seeks to engage a Data Analysis and Validation Officer responsible for ensuring the quality, accuracy, consistency, and reliability of project data. The incumbent will support data validation, quality assurance, database management, monitoring, reporting, and analytical activities to facilitate evidence-based decision-making and effective Programme management.
The position will play a critical role in strengthening data management systems, tracking project achievements, validating beneficiary information, measuring performance indicators, and producing analytical reports in line with UNDP standards and donor requirements.
Scope of work
The Data Analysis and Validation Officer will support programme implementation through systematic data collection, verification, validation, quality assurance, analysis, reporting, and database management. The incumbent will ensure the accuracy and reliability of programme information, support monitoring and evaluation activities, and contribute to evidence-based planning and decision-making.
The position requires close coordination with programme teams, field staff, implementing partners, and beneficiaries to ensure data integrity and compliance with UNDP reporting and accountability requirements.

Duties and Responsibilities
Task Description
1. Technical support and system maintenance
Provide technical assistance to PMU team, maintain and update AIMS systems, and support the use of digital platforms like SharePoint.
2. Data Validation and Quality Assurance
· Verify and validate beneficiary and project data received from field teams and implementing partners.
· Conduct routine data quality assessments to identify inconsistencies, duplicates, missing information, and reporting errors.
· Ensure the accuracy, completeness, and reliability of programme datasets.
· Support beneficiary verification and field validation exercises.
· Develop and maintain data quality control procedures and validation protocols.
· Document validation findings and provide recommendations for corrective actions.
2. Data Management
· Maintain, update, and manage project databases and beneficiary records.
· Clean, organize, and consolidate data collected from multiple sources.
· Ensure secure storage, confidentiality, and accessibility of project data.
· Develop and maintain data tracking systems and reporting templates.
· Support the establishment of standardized data management procedures.
3. Data Analysis and Reporting
· Analyze quantitative and qualitative data to support programme planning and decision-making.
· Produce statistical summaries, trend analyses, beneficiary profiles, and key performance indicators.
· Generate monthly, quarterly, and ad hoc analytical reports.
· Prepare dashboards, presentations, tables, and visual summaries of programme results.
· Provide evidence-based recommendations to support management decisions and programme improvements.
4. Monitoring and Evaluation Support
· Support monitoring and evaluation activities through data validation, analysis, and reporting.
· Track project progress against targets, indicators, and planned results.
· Support baseline assessments, beneficiary surveys, end-line assessments, and other data collection exercises.
· Participate in field monitoring missions and beneficiary verification visits.
· Identify programme trends, implementation gaps, challenges, and lessons learned through data analysis.
5. Coordination and Programme Support
· Coordinate with programme teams, M&E personnel, and implementing partners to improve data quality and reporting processes.
· Support data review meetings and follow up on corrective actions related to data quality issues.
· Assist in preparing programme reports, presentations, and donor reporting materials.
· Participate in meetings with beneficiaries, implementing partners, and UNDP programme teams.
6. Other Duties
· Perform any other duties assigned by the supervisor related to data management, validation, monitoring, analysis, reporting, and programme support.
Institutional arrangement
The Data Analysis and Validation Officer will work under the guidance of the REVIVE Program Manager and report directly to the Technical Specialist - Livelihood. Technical guidance and support will also be provided by the AMIS team.

Job Requirements
Education
A high school education is often the minimum, with a university degree in a related field like IT, Marketing, and Business preferred.
Experience and Skills
· Minimum 3/7 years of relevant experience with a Bachelor's degree or 1 year of experience with a Master's degree.
· Demonstrated experience in data analysis, data validation, monitoring and evaluation, and reporting.
· Experience supporting livelihoods, resilience, recovery, development, or humanitarian programmes.
· Previous experience working with community-based organizations, NGOs, UN agencies, or donor-funded projects is desirable.
· Experience managing large datasets, beneficiary databases, and programme information systems.
Technical aptitude
· Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Office applications.
· Strong knowledge of data cleaning, validation, quality assurance, and statistical analysis.
· Experience using data collection and management platforms such as Kobo Toolbox, ODK, Comcare, or similar tools.
· Familiarity with Power BI or other data visualization platforms is desirable.
· Understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, indicators, and reporting systems
Competencies
· Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
· Excellent attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy.
· Ability to collect, clean, validate, analyze, and interpret complex datasets.
· Strong report writing and presentation skills.
· Ability to identify patterns, trends, and inconsistencies within data.
· Effective communication and interpersonal skills.
· Strong organizational and time-management skills.
· Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a multicultural environment.
· Commitment to confidentiality and responsible data management practices.
Language Requirements
Proficiency in written and spoken English and fluency in local languages, Pashto and Dari is required.

title: Information Technology Advisor
description:
Role Summary
The IT Advisor serves as an independent advisor to the Board of Management and provides strategic guidance, oversight, and recommendations regarding the Bank's information technology environment. The position is responsible for reviewing the effectiveness of IT governance, cybersecurity controls, IT operations, technology risks, digital initiatives, and regulatory compliance, and reporting observations and recommendations directly to the Board of Management.
The IT Advisor shall independently assess the activities, controls, performance, and risk management practices of the Information Technology Department and provide professional advice to support sound decision-making and regulatory compliance.

Duties and Responsibilities
1. IT Governance and Oversight
Review the effectiveness of the Bank's IT governance framework.
Assess whether IT activities are aligned with the Bank's strategic objectives.
Advise the Board of Management on technology-related matters and emerging risks.
Monitor compliance with Board-approved IT policies, procedures, and standards.
Evaluate the adequacy of management oversight over IT operations.
2. IT Risk Management
Review the effectiveness of IT risk management practices.
Assess technology-related risks affecting the Bank's operations.
Advise the Board on significant IT risks and mitigation measures.
Monitor risk indicators relating to cybersecurity, infrastructure, applications, and data management.
Evaluate the Bank's readiness to address technology disruptions and cyber threats.
3. Cybersecurity Oversight
Review cybersecurity controls and security governance practices.
Assess compliance with information security policies and regulatory requirements.
Monitor cybersecurity incidents and corrective actions.
Evaluate vulnerability assessment and penetration testing results.
Advise the Board on cybersecurity improvements and emerging threats.
4. Review of IT Operations
Review the performance and effectiveness of the IT Department.
Assess the adequacy of IT infrastructure, systems, and services.
Monitor system availability, reliability, and operational efficiency.
Evaluate change management, system implementation, and project governance practices.
Review major IT projects and provide recommendations to the Board.
5. Regulatory Compliance
Monitor compliance with Da Afghanistan Bank (DAB) regulations, directives, and guidelines relating to information technology and information security.
Review implementation of regulatory recommendations and audit findings.
Advise the Board regarding regulatory developments affecting technology operations.
6. Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery
Review the effectiveness of business continuity and disaster recovery arrangements.
Assess disaster recovery testing results and corrective actions.
Evaluate the Bank's ability to maintain critical services during disruptions.
Provide recommendations for strengthening operational resilience.
7. Reporting to the Board of Management
Prepare independent reports for the Board of Management regarding:
IT governance effectiveness.
Information security and cybersecurity status.
Technology risks and mitigation measures.
IT operational performance.
Regulatory compliance status.
Significant technology incidents.
Progress of major IT projects.
Present findings, observations, and recommendations during Board meetings.
Escalate significant concerns requiring Board attention.
8. Advisory Role
Provide independent advice on:
Digital transformation initiatives.
Core banking systems.
Information security programs.
Technology investments.
Outsourcing and vendor management.
Emerging technologies and innovation.
Support management and the Board in making informed technology decisions.
9. IT Procurement and Technology Acquisition Oversight
Review and provide independent advice on the procurement of IT hardware, software, licenses, subscriptions, cybersecurity solutions, network equipment, and technology-related services.
Participate in the evaluation and selection process of IT vendors, suppliers, and service providers to ensure transparency, value for money, and alignment with the Bank's strategic objectives.
Assess technical specifications, requirements, and procurement proposals prior to submission for approval.
Ensure that all IT procurements comply with the Bank's procurement policies, information security requirements, and applicable regulatory directives.
Review technology contracts, service-level agreements (SLAs), maintenance agreements, and licensing arrangements from a technical and governance perspective.
Provide recommendations to the Board of Management regarding major technology investments and procurements.
Monitor the implementation and delivery of procured IT solutions to ensure that the Bank receives the agreed products and services.
Advise management and the Board on technology standardization, vendor risks, system compatibility, scalability, and cost optimization.
Participate as a technical advisor in procurement committees whenever technology-related procurements are being evaluated.
Review and advise on all significant technology expenditures, including core banking systems, digital banking platforms, cybersecurity solutions, data center infrastructure, cloud services, and outsourced technology services.

CISA (Certified Information Systems Auditor)
CISM (Certified Information Security Manager)
CISSP (Certified Information Systems Security Professional)
